speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned blisters on your forearm and ulcers on mucosal surfaces; to narrow this down, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you recall any recent sun exposure or new medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris. The combination of new-onset oral/genital ulcers and blisters, alongside a recent history of stopping NSAIDs (meloxicam), is highly suggestive of this autoimmune condition. We do not need further testing to confirm the clinical diagnosis; the next step is to begin immediate treatment with high-dose corticosteroids.
